dedupe_keys.name: global irrigated areas map meier zabel and mauser 2018

description: This global map of irrigated areas at 30 arc-seconds (about 1 km) extends a statistics-based irrigation map with Earth observation. Multi-temporal SPOT-VGT NDVI data and agricultural suitability data, both at 30 arc-seconds, are analysed for 1999 to 2012 in a multiple decision tree, which finds an irrigated area 18% larger than approaches based on statistics, with the largest differences in Asia and particularly China and India, mostly as denser irrigation within already known irrigated regions. It was produced by Jonas Meier, Florian Zabel and Wolfram Mauser and published on PANGAEA in January 2018 as a free download under CC BY-NC 3.0, which excludes commercial use. Caveats: it is a composite for 1999 to 2012, validation showed large divergence among global products, and the method may overestimate irrigation where rainfed crops are very green. Simulation uses: irrigated demand locations for irrigation capacity planning and climate adaptation. Related records: the FAO Global Map of Irrigation Areas (data-fao-global-map-of-irrigation-areas) and GirrEO (data-girreo-global-irrigation-areas-eo).
